question.en: Fill the operator that moves the right pointer one step left.

explanation.en: hi-- decrements the right index so both pointers close in on the middle; hi -= 1 is the same.

question.en: Fill the operator that finds the midpoint without overflowing.

explanation.en: lo + (hi - lo) / 2 is the midpoint; unlike (lo + hi) / 2 it cannot overflow int when both indexes are large.

question.en: Fill the offset of the element that leaves the window.

explanation.en: Sliding the window right adds a[i] and drops a[i - k], the element k places behind it, so each step is O(1).

question.en: Fill the operator that sizes the prefix-sum array.

explanation.en: A prefix array needs n + 1 slots: pre[0] = 0 is the empty prefix, so any range sum is pre[r + 1] - pre[l].

question.en: Fill the HashSet method whose bool result reveals a repeat.

explanation.en: HashSet.Add returns false when the value is already present, so one call both checks and records it.

question.en: Fill the method that returns the size of one dimension of a 2D array.

explanation.en: A rectangular int[,] has one Length for all cells; GetLength(0) is the row count and GetLength(1) the column count.

question.en: Fill the Dictionary method that returns 0 for a missing key.

explanation.en: GetValueOrDefault returns default(int), 0, for an unseen key, so the first occurrence becomes 1 without a KeyNotFoundException.

question.en: Fill the Stack method that removes and returns the top item.

explanation.en: Each closer must match the most recent unmatched opener, and Pop removes it so the next closer sees the one below. Peek would never remove anything.

question.en: Fill the Queue method that takes the next node to visit.

explanation.en: Dequeue removes the oldest node (FIFO), so nodes are expanded in order of distance, which is what makes BFS find shortest edge counts.

question.en: Fill the PriorityQueue method that pops the cheapest entry and ends the loop when empty.

explanation.en: TryDequeue(out element, out priority) returns false once the queue is empty and otherwise hands back the lowest-priority (shortest-distance) entry.

question.en: Fill the method that adds a value with its priority.

explanation.en: PriorityQueue<TElement, TPriority>.Enqueue takes the element and its priority; the smallest priority is dequeued first, so it acts as a min-heap.

question.en: Fill the operator that keeps g[r][c] from being read out of bounds.

explanation.en: || short-circuits: once a bounds test is true the cell is never indexed. A single | evaluates both sides and throws IndexOutOfRangeException at the edge.

question.en: Fill the Dictionary method that checks for a cached result.

explanation.en: ContainsKey tells whether n was already computed, turning the exponential recursion into O(n).

question.en: Fill the keyword that allocates the DP array.

explanation.en: new int[n + 1] allocates n + 1 zeroed ints, one slot per step from 0 to n.

question.en: Fill the Array method that sets every slot to one value.

explanation.en: Array.Fill writes amount + 1 into every slot, a value no real answer can reach, so Math.Min works from the first comparison.

question.en: Fill the method the comparison lambda uses to order two ints.

explanation.en: The Comparison<T> must return negative, zero or positive; int.CompareTo does exactly that, so the array is ordered by start.

question.en: Fill the Array method that flips the order of the characters.

explanation.en: Strings are immutable, so copy them to a char[], reverse it in place with Array.Reverse, and build a new string from it.

question.en: Fill the string method that copies the characters into a mutable array.

explanation.en: ToCharArray returns a new char[] that can be edited in place; the string itself cannot be changed.

question.en: Fill the value that maps a lowercase letter to index 0-25.

explanation.en: char minus char is an int: 'a' - 'a' is 0 and 'z' - 'a' is 25. 97 is the same code point written as a number.

question.en: Fill the bitwise operator that clears the lowest set bit.

explanation.en: n - 1 flips the lowest 1 bit and every 0 below it, so n & (n - 1) drops exactly that bit (Kernighan). The loop runs once per set bit.

question.en: Fill the Math method that decides whether to extend or restart the run.

explanation.en: Math.Max keeps the larger of starting fresh at nums[i] or extending the current run; the best run here is 4, -1, 2, 1 = 6.

question.en: Fill the int constant used as the starting sentinel.

explanation.en: int.MaxValue (2147483647) is larger than every int input, so the first comparison always replaces it.

question.en: Fill the LINQ method that adds up the array.

explanation.en: The numbers 0..n add up to n(n + 1) / 2; subtracting the actual Sum leaves the missing one.

question.en: Fill the Enumerable method that yields 1, 2, 3, 4, 5.

explanation.en: Enumerable.Range(start, count) produces count consecutive ints beginning at start, so (1, 5) is 1 through 5.

question.en: Fill the StringBuilder method that adds each run to the output.

explanation.en: Append adds text to the builder without creating a new string each time, which matters in a loop. AppendLine would add a newline after every run.

question.en: Fill the index that completes the tuple swap.

explanation.en: The right-hand tuple is evaluated first, so (a[i], a[j]) = (a[j], a[i]) swaps without a temporary variable.

question.en: Fill the Span method that views the second half without copying.

explanation.en: Slice(start) returns a Span over the same memory from start to the end, like span[mid..]; no elements are copied.

question.en: Fill the return type that lets this method use yield return.

explanation.en: An iterator method must return IEnumerable<T> (or IEnumerator<T>); returning IEnumerable<long> lets callers use LINQ such as Take(10) on the lazy sequence.

// greatest common divisor (Euclid)
static int Gcd(int a, int b) => b == 0 ? a : Gcd(b, a ____ b);

question.en: Fill the operator in Euclid's step.

explanation.en: gcd(a, b) = gcd(b, a % b); the remainder shrinks every call until it reaches 0, leaving the gcd in a.

question.en: Fill the keyword that skips a repeated anchor value.

explanation.en: After sorting, equal anchors produce the same triplets; continue jumps to the next i. break would stop the whole search early.
